result.title: TDD: Target-Discrepancy Distillation for Underwater Image Enhancement
result.comment: The main paper is 9 pages (including references) with 10 figures. The supplementary material contains 8 pages and 8 additional figures
result.summary: Underwater degradation changes image appearance and can compromise the semantic cues used to guide enhancement. Identifying scene content alone does not explicitly specify the appearance to recover or the input-dependent changes associated with that target. We propose target-discrepancy knowledge distillation (TDD) for underwater image enhancement, which organizes guidance around these two aspects of the same restoration problem. For each degraded-reference training pair, reference features from an underwater vision-language teacher provide target-appearance supervision, while paired feature residuals describe the observation's discrepancy relative to the same target. Both representations are jointly distilled into a lightweight guidance network that predicts them from the degraded image alone; neither the teacher nor reference images are required at inference. To align their use with their supervisory roles, we introduce progressive knowledge fusion within a multi-scale enhancement network. The estimated discrepancy first conditions spatial feature updates, after which target-appearance guidance refines the updated features and channel interactions consolidate their responses. This correction-before-refinement design lets target-guided refinement build on discrepancy-conditioned features. Experiments on six underwater benchmarks demonstrate competitive performance across full-reference and no-reference metrics. Ablations and feature visualizations analyze the contributions of the knowledge source, joint distillation, and progressive fusion.

AI.brief_summary: 提出面向水下图像增强的目标—差异知识蒸馏方法，将视觉语言教师提供的目标外观特征与参考特征残差联合蒸馏到轻量引导网络，并在多尺度增强网络中按“先校正、后细化”的方式融合。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作服务于像素级图像增强，不涉及推理轨迹、latent 推理状态或答案对视觉证据的使用，虽含教师特征蒸馏，但与 LVR 主线缺少可核查的实质联系。
